name: Cordierite
chronometers: Channel H₂O/CO₂ as a fluid record; low-P metamorphic thermobarometry
setting: Cccm (Dana's a and b swapped: (hkl) → (k h l))

matrix.title: Pseudo-hexagonal prism × elongation
matrix.subtitle: Two different orthorhombic prisms both look hexagonal: A = {100}+{110} and B = {010}+{310}, each with faces about 60° apart. Short prisms are capped by c{001} with the pseudo-hexagonal pyramid r{111}+p{201}.
matrix.note: Dana's cell has a and b swapped relative to the structure, so his b(010) cleavage is (100) here. Pyramid angles match Dana to within 0.1°, but the prism angle is 1.5° off because Miller's 1850s axial ratios are imprecise. Sector trillings are not modelled.

about: Cordierite is orthorhombic, but a ≈ √3·b makes it pseudo-hexagonal. That is why crystals look like short hexagonal prisms, and why cyclic sector trillings with a hexagonal outline are common. Trillings have been read as inversion from hexagonal indialite or as rapid, overstepped growth (Putnis & Holland 1986; Kitamura & Yamada 1987). Molecules trapped in its ring channels record metamorphic fluids.

habits.name: Short pseudo-hexagonal prism
habits.text: c with prism A or B (rows L1–L2).

habits.name: With dipyramid
habits.text: Bevelled by the pseudo-hexagonal r + p pyramid.

habits.name: Sector trilling (not modelled)
habits.text: A cyclic twin with six sectors.

references.citation: Malcherek, T., Domeneghetti, M.C., Tazzoli, V., Ottolini, L., McCammon, C., Carpenter, M.A. (2001). Structural properties of ferromagnesian cordierites. American Mineralogist 86, 66–79.
Putnis, A., Holland, T.J.B. (1986). Sector trilling in cordierite and equilibrium overstepping in metamorphism. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 93, 265–272.
references.note: Links trilling morphology to overstepped growth.

references.citation: Kitamura, M., Yamada, H. (1987). Origin of sector trilling in cordierite in Daimonji hornfels, Kyoto, Japan. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 97, 1–6.
references.note: Sector-trilling cordierite in a contact aureole.

references.citation: Kitamura, M., Hiroi, Y. (1982). Indialite from Unazuki pelitic schist, Japan, and its transition texture to cordierite. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 80, 110–116.
references.note: Hexagonal-to-orthorhombic transition texture, the origin of the pseudo-hexagonal habit.
